==English==
{{wp}}
[[Image:PorcheCentralNordCathedraleChartre041130-.jpg|thumb|Portal of Chartres Cathedral]]
[[File:Bramhope Tunnel north portal 1b.jpg|thumb|The north '''portal''' of [[Bramhope]] Tunnel, north of [[Leeds]], England]]

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per- (fare)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|portal}}, {{m|enm|porttol}}, from {{der|en|fro|portal}} and {{der|en|la-med|portāle}}, from {{m|la|porta}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɔːtl̩/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɔɹtl̩/|[ˈpʰɔɹɾɫ̩]|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-portal.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|por|tal}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)təl|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# An entrance, entry point, or means of entry.
#: {{ux|en|The local library, a '''portal''' of knowledge.}}
## A large primary [[adit]] as the main entrance to a [[mine#Noun|mine]].
# {{lb|en|Internet}} A {{l|en|website}} or {{l|en|page}} that acts as an entrance to other websites or pages on the Internet.
#: {{ux|en|The new medical '''portal''' has dozens of topical categories containing links to hundreds of sites.}}
## {{lb|en|Philippines}} An [[ePortal]]. {{gl|a web-based platform that serves as a gateway to various resources, services, or information, usually tailored for specific organizational or user needs.}}
##: {{ux|en|I have already inputted my info on the '''portal'''.}}
## {{lb|en|Philippines}} The existence of an [[account]] on an ePortal.
##: {{ux|en|You need to have a '''portal''' to have a driver's license.}}
# {{lb|en|anatomy}} A short {{l|en|artery}} that carries {{l|en|blood}} into the [[liver]].
# {{lb|en|science fiction|and|fantasy}} A magical or technological {{l|en|aperture}} leading to another location, period in time, or dimension.
#* {{RQ:FT|title=The pandemic is a portal|date=Apr 3 2020|author=w:Arundhati Roy|url=https://www.ft.com/content/10d8f5e8-74eb-11ea-95fe-fcd274e920ca|passage=Historically, pandemics have forced humans to break with the past and imagine their world anew. This one is no different. It is a '''portal''', a gateway between one world and the next.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260424204901/https://www.ft.com/content/10d8f5e8-74eb-11ea-95fe-fcd274e920ca|archivedate=24 April 2026}}
# {{lb|en|architecture}} A lesser gate, where there are two of different dimensions.
# {{lb|en|architecture}} Formerly, a small square corner in a room separated from the rest of an [[apartment]] by [[wainscoting]], forming a short [[passage]] to another apartment.
# A [[grandiose]] and often [[lavish]] [[entrance]].
#: {{cot|en|gate#Noun}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=3|passage=Thick with sparkling orient gems / The '''portal''' shone.|year=1873}}
# {{lb|en|bridge-building}} The space, at one end, between [[opposite]] [[truss]]es when these are [[terminate]]d by [[inclined]] [[brace]]s.
# A [[prayer book]] or [[breviary]]; a [[portass]].
# {{lb|en|US|_|college sports}} The NCAA transfer portal, a database and compliance tool designed to facilitate student-athletes who wish to change schools.
# {{lb|en|computer graphics}} A connecting window between volumes, in [[portal rendering]].
